text: The industry-standard thickness of the silicon device layer used for silicon photonic integrated circuits at 1550 nm is:
explanation: The 220 nm silicon-on-insulator device layer is the photonics standard, balancing single-mode operation, high confinement (~0.8), and manageable two-photon absorption. 45 nm is an advanced CMOS transistor node; 2 um is the buried-oxide (BOX) thickness; 450 nm is the standard single-mode strip width, not the layer thickness.
